The disclosure relates to an imaging apparatus, an image sensor, and an image processing unit designed to reduce the computational workload associated with image recognition. The image sensor includes photoelectric conversion elements arranged across an imaging surface. These elements convert incident light into electrical pixel signals, which are then used to generate image data.

To support efficient image recognition, the imaging surface is divided into multiple areas. The image sensor generates image recognition support information independently for each area, allowing relevant image characteristics to be identified at a localized level. The image processing unit then uses this support information to apply predetermined processing to the corresponding image data. By performing part of the analysis within the image sensor, the system reduces the amount of processing required from the image processing unit and can improve the speed and efficiency of image recognition.

This technology may be incorporated into various imaging devices, including cameras equipped with face detection functionality. In such applications, the area-specific support information can help the image processing unit identify and process regions likely to contain a face, thereby enabling faster and more efficient detection.
outputs.L4:
The disclosure relates to an imaging apparatus designed to perform image-recognition processing more efficiently. The apparatus includes an image sensor having an imaging surface on which a plurality of pixels are arranged. The imaging surface is divided into multiple areas, and pixel signals are obtained for each area when an image is captured.

In addition to generating image data, the image sensor analyzes the pixel signals associated with the respective areas and generates recognition-support information. This information may represent characteristics useful for identifying objects or regions within the captured image, such as brightness distributions, color information, edge components, contrast, or other image features. The recognition-support information is supplied to an image-processing unit together with, or separately from, the captured image data.

The image-processing unit uses the support information to perform recognition tasks such as detecting a person’s face, locating a subject, identifying an object, or determining a region of interest. Because the sensor has already extracted information relevant to recognition on an area-by-area basis, the image-processing unit does not need to analyze every pixel of the full image from the beginning. It can instead prioritize selected areas, narrow the search range, or use the supplied feature information as an initial input for subsequent recognition processing.

Generating recognition-support information within the image sensor therefore distributes the processing workload between the sensor and the image-processing unit. This arrangement reduces the computational burden placed on the image-processing unit, shortens recognition time, and may lower power consumption and memory-transfer requirements. As a result, the imaging apparatus can perform image analysis and subject recognition more rapidly and efficiently, including in applications that require continuous or real-time processing.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can mean any book, while “the book” refers to a particular one.

Although it is easy to overlook, “the” gives language clarity and precision. It helps listeners and readers understand that something is already known, unique, or especially significant. In phrases such as “the sun,” “the truth,” or “the future,” this simple word directs attention toward a shared concept.

“The” demonstrates how even the shortest words can carry great meaning. Without it, English would feel less natural, less exact, and much harder to understand.

counterfactuals.output: An imaging apparatus includes an image sensor and an image processor. counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention involving a two-dimensional photoelectric image sensor that divides its imaging surface into multiple regions and outputs per-region support data for downstream image recognition, such as face detection.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a two-dimensional photoelectric image sensor whose pixel array is logically divided into multiple regions. In addition to ordinary pixel-image data, the sensor aggregates measurements within each region—such as luminance, color components, contrast, edge strength, or other feature statistics—and outputs these as per-region “support data.”

A downstream recognition processor uses the support data to identify promising areas of the image before performing more computationally expensive analysis. For example, in face detection, it may select regions having skin-tone color, suitable brightness, or face-like contrast patterns and then apply detailed recognition only to those regions.

By generating the regional statistics in or near the sensor, the invention reduces transferred data, narrows the recognition search area, lowers processing load and power consumption, and can accelerate real-time image recognition.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in the language of a patent application, a camera with a face detection function that reduces image-processing workload by calculating recognition support information directly within the image sensor.
counterfactuals.output:
### Title  
**Imaging Apparatus Including Image Sensor Configured to Generate Face-Recognition Support Information**

### Abstract  
An imaging apparatus includes an image sensor and an image-processing circuit. The image sensor includes a pixel array configured to generate image signals and an in-sensor processing circuit configured to calculate recognition support information from the image signals. The recognition support information may include one or more of luminance statistics, chrominance statistics, edge information, feature values, skin-color likelihood values, spatial frequency information, reduced-resolution image data, or candidate-region information. The image-processing circuit performs face detection using the recognition support information received from the image sensor. Because at least a portion of the information used for face detection is calculated within the image sensor, transfer of full-resolution image data and execution of corresponding processing by the image-processing circuit may be reduced, thereby decreasing processing workload, power consumption, memory bandwidth, and face-detection latency.

### Detailed Description  
In one embodiment, an imaging apparatus comprises an image sensor, a controller, and an image-processing circuit. The image sensor includes a two-dimensional pixel array having a plurality of photoelectric conversion elements. The pixel array captures light from a subject and outputs pixel signals corresponding to an image of the subject.

The image sensor further includes a processing circuit formed on the same semiconductor substrate as the pixel array or on a semiconductor layer electrically coupled to the pixel array in a stacked configuration. The processing circuit receives pixel signals from the pixel array and calculates recognition support information before, during, or independently of transmission of captured image data to the image-processing circuit.

The recognition support information is information usable to identify an image region likely to include a human face. By way of example, the recognition support information may comprise:

- a reduced-resolution representation of the captured image;
- luminance or color histograms for respective image regions;
- skin-tone likelihood values;
- horizontal, vertical, or directional edge values;
- local contrast or texture values;
- feature descriptors;
- motion information derived from successive image frames;
- coordinates and confidence values of candidate face regions; or
- combinations thereof.

In an exemplary operation, the in-sensor processing circuit divides an imaging area into a plurality of blocks and calculates, for each block, one or more feature values based on the corresponding pixel signals. The in-sensor processing circuit may compare the feature values with predetermined conditions to select one or more candidate regions. Information identifying the candidate regions is transmitted to the image-processing circuit as metadata associated with the captured image.

The image-processing circuit performs a face-detection process preferentially on the candidate regions rather than searching the entirety of the full-resolution image. Alternatively, the image-processing circuit may perform an initial face-detection stage using only the recognition support information and subsequently access full-resolution pixel data for regions determined to have a face likelihood exceeding a threshold.

The controller may cause the image sensor to change the type, spatial resolution, frame rate, or calculation precision of the recognition support information according to an operating state of the imaging apparatus. For example, low-resolution support information may be generated continuously during a preview operation, while higher-resolution support information may be generated after detection of a candidate face or upon receipt of an image-capture instruction.

Because preliminary feature extraction and/or candidate-region determination is performed within the image sensor, the amount of pixel data transferred to an external image processor may be reduced. Moreover, computationally expensive processing of image regions unlikely to contain a face may be omitted. The disclosed configuration therefore reduces image-processing workload and may improve power efficiency, processing speed, and responsiveness of autofocus, automatic exposure, subject tracking, and other functions based on face detection.

### Exemplary Claim  
1. **An imaging apparatus comprising:**  
   an image sensor including:  
   a pixel array configured to generate pixel signals representing a captured image; and  
   an in-sensor processing circuit configured to calculate, from the pixel signals, recognition support information indicative of a likelihood that at least one region of the captured image includes a face; and  
   an image-processing circuit configured to receive the recognition support information from the image sensor and perform face detection based at least in part on the recognition support information,  
   wherein the recognition support information enables the image-processing circuit to limit face-detection processing to a subset of the captured image, thereby reducing an image-processing workload.
